explanation: Potters painted cobalt oxide onto the porcelain under a clear glaze before firing. Under the Yuan and early Ming dynasties much of the cobalt was imported from Persia.

claims.text: Chinese blue-and-white porcelain is painted with a cobalt oxide pigment.
The blue of Chinese blue-and-white porcelain is not made with copper, lapis lazuli or indigo.
Blue-and-white decoration was painted under a clear glaze before the porcelain was fired.
Much of the cobalt used for Yuan and early Ming blue-and-white porcelain was imported from Persia.
